introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Religious Studies 2 (0785), Paper 2: The Old Testament/Islam and African Traditional Religious Beliefs and Practices. ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2019. Duration: three hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR questions chosen from any ONE SECTION ONLY. All questions carry equal marks.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Le sujet fait deux pages (page de garde et liste des 18 questions), scanné, avec filigrane gcerevision.com sans incidence sur la lecture ; aucune figure.

As the first king in Israel, Saul failed to live up to God's expectations. » est coupé sur deux lignes, avec deux mentions « (25 marks) ». La Q6 est imprimée sans verbe de consigne (probablement « Discuss » omis) : le corrigé la traite en « discuss » et le dit. Lecture à confirmer sur un exemplaire papier.

Coquilles du sujet corrigées dans la transcription : Q2 guillemet ouvrant manquant (« God can write straight on crooked lines' ») ; Q3 « life off the Israelites » transcrit « life of the Israelites » ; Q11 « Surah 109 (A1 -Kafirun) » transcrit « (Al-Kafirun) » ; Q16 point final doublé (« claim. . ») ; l'intitulé de section imprimé « Sectionl.lThe Patriarchs to David » est lu « Section 1.1 The Patriarchs to David » (au-dessus : « 1.0 The OLD TESTAMENT/JEWISH BIBLE »).

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées de mémoire, sans accès à une source. Les références bibliques citées (Genèse 12, 15, 17, 25, 27-29, 32-33, 37, 50 ; Exode 19-20, 24, 32, 34 ; 1 Samuel 1-3, 7-13, 15-16, 22, 28, 31 ; Jérémie 31 ; Genèse 22) sont des passages classiques ; les numéros de versets précis ne sont donnés que pour des textes très connus. Aucune référence n'est inventée.

Section Islam (Q7-12) : exposé du fiqh sunnite courant ; les écoles juridiques divergent sur plusieurs points de la Q7 (injections, gouttes pour les yeux, inhalateurs, émission volontaire sans rapport sexuel, tabac) et le corrigé le dit. Q9 : l'identité du fils sacrifié (Ismaël selon la tradition musulmane majoritaire, non nommé par le Coran) est présentée prudemment ; la date de l'institution de la fête est donnée « selon la tradition ». Q10 : positions des savants courants, sans attribution à un texte précis au-delà de Coran 5:32, 2:190 et 2:256, versets très connus. Q11 : l'occasion de la révélation de la sourate 109 est rapportée « selon la tradition islamique » ; renvois à 2:256, 60:8 et 6:108 (versets bien établis). Q12 : l'imamat chiite est mentionné de façon descriptive (chiisme duodécimain), sans jugement.

Section ATR (Q13-18) : généralités tirées des auteurs classiques du programme (Mbiti en particulier : « I am because we are... », « living-dead ») ; les croyances varient selon les peuples et le corrigé le dit. Exemples cités avec prudence : Obatala et Olodumare chez les Yoruba (Q13), « chi » chez les Igbo (Q15). Aucune tradition locale camerounaise n'est inventée.

Thèmes nouveaux créés pour ce paper (aucun autre dossier Religious Studies n'existait au moment de la transcription) : « mosque and the ummah », « islam and terrorism », « islam and other faiths », « imamate and leadership in islam », « atr myths and oral tradition », « atr worship and sacrifice », « atr community and the individual », « atr marriage and family », « atr death and the afterlife ». questions.enonce_markdown:
Marriage and procreation are inseparable in ATR. Justify this claim.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** In most African traditional societies, marriage is not simply a union of two individuals but a union of two families and a religious and social duty. Its main purpose is the bringing forth of children. The claim that marriage and procreation are inseparable is therefore largely justified. The points are general and vary among peoples.

**1. Marriage is a duty and a stage of life.** Mbiti and other writers observe that in ATR every normal person is expected to marry. The unmarried adult is seen as incomplete, and marriage is the gateway through which a person becomes a full member of the community.

**2. Children continue the family and the community.** The lineage survives only through the birth of children. A person without a descendant is thought to risk being forgotten: children keep the name alive, look after the parents in old age and, after death, remember them and honour them, which maintains the dead person's place among the ancestors.

**3. Children are a sign of blessing.** They are regarded as gifts of God and the ancestors, and a large family is a mark of honour, strength and wealth. Many names express gratitude for children.

**4. Rebirth of ancestors.** In many communities a newborn child is believed to carry the spirit or character of an ancestor, so procreation is a way in which the ancestors come back to the living family.

**5. Rites connect marriage to procreation.** Fertility is promoted by prayers, libations and sacrifices to God and the ancestors, by blessings given at the wedding and by rituals during pregnancy and birth. Bridewealth (dowry) is often understood as a compensation to the wife's family for the loss of her child-bearing and work, and its payment gives the husband the right to the children.

**6. Barrenness is a serious problem.** Childlessness is treated as a calamity, and remedies are sought: consulting diviners, offering sacrifices, using herbs, adopting children, taking a second wife or other arrangements such as levirate custom. In some societies childlessness is a reason for divorce or remarriage. The fact that such efforts are made shows that marriage is not complete without children.

**7. Sexual relations are sacred.** Sexual union is carefully regulated by taboos and it is for the purpose of begetting life, which is a reflection of God's work of creation; intercourse outside marriage is generally discouraged.

**Qualification.** Love, companionship and economic cooperation also matter, and in practice many couples without children remain together; modern education and religions are changing attitudes. Nevertheless, traditional thought places procreation at the heart of marriage.

**Conclusion.** Because marriage serves to perpetuate the lineage, to honour the ancestors and to bring blessings, procreation is its main purpose, and the claim is justified.
